identity.subject: PHYSICS
identity.canonical_name: Thermodynamics — research-depth discovery and reconciliation pilot
identity.identity_rationale: A bounded non-runtime diversity pilot for current Grade XI thermodynamics scope, evidence depth, prerequisites, applicability conditions and research-overlay invariance.

includes.statement: Current CBSE Grade XI Thermodynamics core: thermal equilibrium and temperature, zeroth law, heat, work, internal energy, first and second laws, thermodynamic state variables and equation of state, and isothermal, adiabatic, reversible, irreversible and cyclic processes.
Research-depth engineering of the core includes explicit system boundary, sign convention, state-versus-process distinctions and applicability conditions needed to prevent invalid equation use.
Research-depth evidence may add population-limited learner-difficulty findings and advanced explanatory checks without mutating the confirmed curriculum core.

excludes.statement: Entropy formalism is not promoted as an explicit current CBSE Grade XI Thermodynamics requirement by this pilot; it remains research/advanced context unless separately authorized.
Carnot cycles, heat-engine efficiency, enthalpy and Gibbs free energy are not silently promoted into the current CBSE Grade XI Physics Thermodynamics core by research sources or adjacent disciplines.

unresolved_boundaries.detail: The shared CrossDomain provider registry routes Mathematics through the existing Grade 9 provider root, while this pilot targets Grade XI; no Grade XI provider-owned readiness receipt exists here.

curriculum_bindings.rationale: The official current CBSE Physics curriculum explicitly names Unit VIII / Chapter 11 Thermodynamics and enumerates the included laws, state-variable/equation-of-state language and process types.
exclusions: External assessment coverage and university thermodynamics sources cannot add curriculum-required topics.

capabilities.title: Reason with thermal equilibrium and the zeroth law
capabilities.disciplinary_meaning: Identify thermal-equilibrium relations and use the zeroth law to connect equilibrium with a consistent temperature concept without importing unrelated microscopic assumptions.
capabilities.learner_success_statement: Can identify when bodies are in mutual thermal equilibrium and explain what the zeroth law permits one to infer about temperature.
capabilities.granularity_rationale: The curriculum explicitly separates thermal equilibrium/temperature and the zeroth law as core thermodynamic ideas.

capabilities.title: Apply the first law with an explicit system and sign convention
capabilities.disciplinary_meaning: Account for change in internal energy from heat transfer and work after declaring the thermodynamic system and a consistent work-sign convention.
capabilities.learner_success_statement: Can define the system, identify heat and work transfers, state the sign convention, apply the first law and interpret the resulting change in internal energy.
capabilities.granularity_rationale: Heat, work, internal energy and the first law form one tightly coupled accounting capability whose validity depends on system and sign semantics.

capabilities.title: Classify thermodynamic states and processes
capabilities.disciplinary_meaning: Distinguish state variables from transfer/path quantities and apply the defining constraints of isothermal, adiabatic, cyclic, reversible and irreversible processes without treating labels as sufficient proof.
capabilities.learner_success_statement: Can identify relevant state variables, classify a process from its declared constraints and state which thermodynamic quantities are constrained or not constrained by that classification.
capabilities.granularity_rationale: The current curriculum explicitly names thermodynamic state variables/equation of state and five process classes; research evidence shows context-sensitive state/path confusion.

capabilities.title: Use the second law to constrain process direction and reversibility
capabilities.disciplinary_meaning: Use second-law reasoning to distinguish idealized reversible behavior from irreversible behavior and reject process descriptions that rely on first-law conservation alone.
capabilities.learner_success_statement: Can explain why energy conservation by itself does not determine thermodynamic direction and can distinguish reversible from irreversible process descriptions at the curriculum level.
capabilities.granularity_rationale: The second law and reversible/irreversible distinction are explicit curriculum requirements but deeper entropy formalism is deliberately separated as research context.

capabilities.title: Connect mechanical work to thermodynamic work
capabilities.disciplinary_meaning: Carry the energy-transfer meaning of work from mechanics into a system-boundary description while recognizing that thermodynamic sign conventions must be declared explicitly.
capabilities.learner_success_statement: Can relate mechanical work to energy transfer across a thermodynamic boundary and avoid equating work with a stored state variable.
capabilities.granularity_rationale: Work and energy precede thermodynamics in the same Grade XI curriculum and provide a structural bridge into first-law reasoning.

capabilities.title: Connect thermal-properties temperature concepts to thermodynamics
capabilities.disciplinary_meaning: Use prior temperature and heat concepts as prerequisites without treating heat as a substance or as a state variable of the system.
capabilities.learner_success_statement: Can use temperature and heat-transfer language consistently when entering thermodynamic equilibrium and energy-accounting problems.
capabilities.granularity_rationale: Thermal Properties of Matter immediately precedes Thermodynamics in the current Grade XI Physics curriculum and supplies necessary vocabulary and phenomena.

prerequisite_edges.rationale: First-law work terms require an energy-transfer interpretation of work that is structurally inherited from the earlier Work, Energy and Power unit.
The current sequence places thermal properties, including heat and temperature, immediately before thermodynamics; equilibrium reasoning uses those prior concepts.
A pressure-volume representation can require interpreting signed area or an integral as work; this pilot does not self-certify the Mathematics capability or its Grade XI readiness.

obligations.selection_policy: Use the exact current official CBSE Physics curriculum version for Grade XI scope; external exams and advanced references cannot replace it.
Use authoritative disciplinary references with explicit system, state, work/heat and applicability semantics; preserve sign-convention differences explicitly.
Retain the exact sign convention, boundary assumptions and process assumptions attached to any formal relation or graphical work interpretation.
Use peer-reviewed evidence with population and task context; do not promote university-population findings as canonical Grade XI misconceptions.
Use the exact official NTA JEE Main syllabus only as external assessment evidence; it must not rewrite CBSE curriculum truth.
Research-only claims remain additive to a frozen base-claim snapshot and require explicit source and applicability records.

source_ledger.title: CBSE Physics (Code No. 042) Class XI curriculum 2026-27

intent_assessments.selection_reason: This is the official current CBSE Physics curriculum and explicitly enumerates Unit VIII / Chapter 11 Thermodynamics for Class XI 2026-27.
limitations: Curriculum wording establishes scope, not detailed derivations or empirical learner-conception claims.

intent_assessments.selection_reason: This is the official NTA JEE Main 2026 syllabus and directly records external assessment coverage of thermodynamics concepts.
limitations: JEE Main assessment coverage does not define or supersede CBSE curriculum truth.

source_ledger.title: MIT Unified Engineering Thermodynamics — First Law of Thermodynamics

intent_assessments.selection_reason: MIT's thermodynamics reference explicitly distinguishes internal energy as a state property and states the first-law energy balance with a declared work-by-system convention.
limitations: University engineering treatment exceeds Grade XI depth and does not define CBSE scope.

intent_assessments.selection_reason: The source states the first-law relation and connects thermodynamic work to process descriptions with explicit conventions and model conditions.
limitations: Any pressure-volume work relation must retain its boundary/quasi-static assumptions rather than becoming a universal formula.

source_ledger.title: MIT OpenCourseWare Thermodynamics and Kinetics lecture sequence

intent_assessments.selection_reason: The MIT sequence explicitly separates state/zeroth law, work/heat/first law, adiabatic changes, second law, entropy and irreversibility, making advanced dependencies auditable.
limitations: Undergraduate chemistry/physics treatment is not Grade XI curriculum authority and includes topics beyond current CBSE scope.

intent_assessments.selection_reason: The source provides an authoritative advanced explanation of entropy and irreversibility while remaining explicitly outside the base curriculum claim set.
limitations: Research-extension promotion cannot mutate the frozen STANDARD base claim snapshot.

source_ledger.title: Investigating introductory and advanced students' difficulties with change in internal energy, work, and heat transfer using a validated instrument

intent_assessments.selection_reason: Peer-reviewed study uses a validated thermodynamics instrument across more than 1000 students in 12 introductory and advanced physics classes and documents difficulties with internal energy, work and heat transfer.
limitations: Population is U.S. higher-education physics, not CBSE Grade XI; the pilot therefore treats the observed reasoning as transfer-limited evidence, not a canonical Grade XI misconception.
intent_assessments.population_context: More than 1000 students across 12 introductory and advanced physics classes at four U.S. public higher-education institutions

source_ledger.title: Investigating the impact of problem properties on introductory and advanced student responses to introductory thermodynamics conceptual problems

intent_assessments.selection_reason: Peer-reviewed research directly studies problem-context dependence for state variables, path-dependent heat/work and signed pressure-volume area interpretation using a validated survey.
limitations: Population is introductory and advanced university physics; findings must not be generalized automatically to Grade XI learners.
intent_assessments.population_context: Introductory and advanced university physics students after traditional lecture-based thermodynamics instruction

intent_assessments.selection_reason: The study explicitly tests signed pressure-volume area interpretation and therefore provides representation-specific difficulty evidence rather than general representation authority.
limitations: Evidence supports a candidate representation obligation, not a universal mandate that every learner artifact use a pressure-volume graph.
intent_assessments.population_context: Introductory and advanced university physics students

source_ledger.title: Investigating introductory and advanced students' difficulties with entropy and the second law of thermodynamics using a validated instrument

intent_assessments.selection_reason: Peer-reviewed validated-instrument research reports a widespread tendency among introductory students to reason as though entropy were conserved.
limitations: Population is U.S. higher education, not CBSE Grade XI; entropy formalism is also not promoted here as an explicit current CBSE core requirement.
intent_assessments.population_context: More than 1000 students across introductory and advanced physics classes at four U.S. public higher-education institutions

concepts.title: Thermodynamic system and state
concepts.disciplinary_meaning: A thermodynamic description is attached to a declared system and its state; state properties are distinguished from energy transferred during a process.

concepts.title: Internal energy as a state property
concepts.disciplinary_meaning: Internal energy is a property of the thermodynamic state; heat transfer and work are process transfers that can change it rather than stored state variables called heat or work.

concepts.title: Thermodynamic process and constraints
concepts.disciplinary_meaning: A thermodynamic process connects states under declared constraints; labels such as isothermal, adiabatic, cyclic, reversible and irreversible carry different physical conditions and consequences.

relations.title: First-law energy balance with work-by-system convention
relations.meaning: For the declared convention, change in internal energy equals heat transferred into the system minus work done by the system; changing convention requires changing the algebra consistently.

applicability_conditions.statement: The thermodynamic system and boundary are declared.
Positive W_by denotes work done by the system and the same convention is used throughout the calculation.

relations.title: State-property closure over a cycle
relations.formal_expression: cycle returns to initial state => Delta U_cycle = 0
relations.meaning: Because internal energy is a state property, its net change is zero when a cyclic process returns the system to the same state; heat and work over the cycle need not individually vanish.

applicability_conditions.statement: The final thermodynamic state is the same as the initial state.

representations.title: System-boundary energy-transfer diagram
representations.purpose: Make the chosen system explicit and separate energy transfer by heat and work from the internal-energy state property.
translation_invariants: heat and work arrows denote transfers, not stored state variables

representations.title: Pressure-volume process graph
representations.purpose: Represent thermodynamic states and process paths and support research-depth reasoning about path dependence and mechanical work where the model permits it.
translation_invariants: axis quantities and direction must remain explicit
process path must not be replaced by endpoint information alone

potential_loss: path geometry and signed-area information can be lost in a purely symbolic balance

representations.title: First-law symbolic balance
representations.purpose: Encode the energy balance only after the system and sign convention are declared.
translation_invariants: work sign convention must remain explicit
Delta U remains a state change while Q and W remain transfers

steps.semantic_job: Declare the system, boundary and initial/final states before assigning heat or work terms.

subject_transition.statement: From verbal situation to a declared thermodynamic system.

steps.fragility_rationale: System ambiguity changes the meaning of every transfer term.

steps.semantic_job: Declare the work-sign convention before writing the first-law balance.

subject_transition.statement: Bind verbal work direction to the chosen algebraic sign convention.

steps.fragility_rationale: Different references use different work sign conventions, so an undeclared sign can reverse the physical interpretation.

steps.semantic_job: Identify only the constraints actually licensed by the process description and distinguish state properties from path-dependent transfers.

subject_transition.statement: From process label or graph to explicit physical constraints.

steps.fragility_rationale: Validated university studies show strong context dependence in state/path and process reasoning; the Grade XI transfer remains a research hypothesis.

steps.semantic_job: Apply the first law with only the justified heat, work and state-change information.

subject_transition.statement: From physical transfers and constraints to an energy balance.

steps.fragility_rationale: Research documents cases where students treat no heat transfer as no internal-energy change and omit work entirely.

steps.semantic_job: Use second-law and reversibility reasoning as a plausibility constraint rather than assuming energy conservation determines process direction.

subject_transition.statement: From energy-consistent result to thermodynamic directionality check.

steps.fragility_rationale: Entropy/second-law studies show productive and unproductive reasoning can diverge even when first-law accounting is correct.

checks.statement: Verify that the chosen system boundary is explicit and unchanged before interpreting heat, work or internal-energy terms.
checks.acceptance_condition: All transfer directions and state quantities refer to the same declared system.
checks.independence_rationale: Boundary identity is checked against the physical model rather than by reproducing the algebra.

checks.statement: Verify that the first-law energy balance is consistent with the declared sign convention and transfer directions.
checks.acceptance_condition: Delta U equals heat into the system minus work by the system under the declared convention.
checks.independence_rationale: This is a direct conservation recheck of the governing balance, not an alternate derivation.

checks.statement: For a claimed cycle, verify that returning to the same state gives zero net change in internal energy.
checks.acceptance_condition: A closed state cycle has Delta U_cycle equal to zero while heat and work may remain nonzero and balance each other.
checks.independence_rationale: State closure supplies a separate endpoint check on the energy accounting.

checks.statement: Verify that a pressure-volume graph preserves axis meaning, path direction and any signed-area interpretation used in reasoning.
checks.acceptance_condition: The graphical interpretation does not discard path information or reverse the declared work direction.
checks.independence_rationale: The graph is checked semantically rather than by comparing with the final numeric answer.

problem_families.title: System-boundary first-law and process reasoning
problem_families.structural_signature: A declared thermodynamic system undergoes a specified or represented process; the solver must identify valid process constraints, distinguish state change from heat/work transfer, apply energy accounting, and check physical direction or cycle closure.

allowed_variations.invariant: Only explicitly licensed process constraints may be used.
System identity, state/path distinction and sign convention remain explicit.

near_transfer: change numerical values or process labels while retaining the same system-boundary and first-law structure
far_transfer: compare multiple paths between the same states or reason about an unfamiliar cyclic process

base_claim_snapshot.statement: The current CBSE Grade XI Thermodynamics core explicitly includes thermal equilibrium/temperature, zeroth law, heat, work, internal energy, first and second laws, thermodynamic state variable/equation of state, and isothermal, adiabatic, reversible, irreversible and cyclic processes.
Under the declared work-by-system convention used by this pilot, the first-law balance is Delta U = Q_in - W_by.
Internal energy is treated as a state property while heat transfer and work describe process transfers; process constraints determine which terms or changes may be inferred.

research_extension_claims.statement: Entropy-based formulations provide a deeper account of irreversibility and second-law directionality, but this pilot does not promote entropy formalism as an explicit current CBSE Grade XI Thermodynamics requirement.

Pressure-volume graph area can encode thermodynamic work under appropriate model/process conditions; representation-specific evidence shows that signed-area interpretation is a distinct reasoning demand.

learner_conception_candidates.statement: Treating an adiabatic process as implying zero change in internal energy because there is no heat transfer, while ignoring work.
Reasoning as though entropy were conserved, with every entropy increase requiring an equal decrease elsewhere.

discovery_reconciliation.target: Grade XI Physics thermodynamics base package

architecture_findings.detail: The current Physics generation manifest explicitly declares Grade 9 while the current official Thermodynamics curriculum target is Grade XI; AgentTasks must expose and hold this mismatch rather than treating subject identity alone as sufficient authority.

The SKP prerequisite contract uses CAP-* capability IDs while the current CrossDomain provider registry routes subject prerequisites by prefixes such as MATH-; a future adapter/identifier policy is required before provider-ready closure can be claimed for this external Mathematics prerequisite.
The roadmap research_overlay module remains PLANNED, so research claims are recorded as pilot-only additive claim records and cannot become a production overlay.
